notes: Live research (Oct 2026): The listed URL https://www.uni-graz.at/en/studies/scholarships returns HTTP 404; the live equivalent funding hub is https://www.uni-graz.at/en/study/studying-at-the-university-of-graz/financing-your-studies/, which states: 'You can apply for a merit-based scholarship if you meet the requirements specified by the relevant faculty' and that merit scholarships 'can be awarded, on application, to students with Austrian citizenship, EEA citizens as well as stateless persons and refugees'. Details are administered by the faculty Dean's offices; the same tuition-fee hub (https://studienabteilung.uni-graz.at/en/tuition-fee/grants-and-scholarships) confirms 'Promotional and Merit Scholarships - You can get information ... at the Dean's office' and points national schemes to the Austrian Study Grant Authority and grants.at. The university's international page (https://welcome.uni-graz.at/en/international-students/prospective-students) even states: 'The University of Graz does not currently award scholarships for international students.' No supervising professor, lab or research group is named anywhere on the official pages; only administrative contacts (4students@uni-graz.at, international.students@uni-graz.at). Faculty-allocated merit scholarships have no individual faculty tie, so no professor entry can be evidenced.

Live research (Oct 2026): The listed URL https://www.uibk.ac.at/en/studies/scholarships returns HTTP 404; the live official pages are https://www.uibk.ac.at/en/college-service-center/scholarships/performance-based-scholarships and https://www.uibk.ac.at/en/college-service-center/scholarships/scholarships-for-scientific-theses. Performance scholarships are awarded under §57 StudFG to Austrian/EEA citizens and applications go through 'LFU:online' and the College Service Center, whose only published contact is the administrative office 'fakultaetenservicestelle@uibk.ac.at'. The thesis-scholarship call requires only a generic 'expert opinion from a university teacher (as set out in § 94 Paragraph 2 of the Universities Act 2002)' - no named supervisor. The related university doctoral scholarship (https://www.uibk.ac.at/en/research/research-funding/phd/doctoral-scholarship) likewise refers generically to 'the dissertation supervisor' for progress reports, with admin contact forschungsfoerderung@uibk.ac.at. No individual professor is named or tied to the scholarship on any official page.

Live research (Oct 2026): The official EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue (https://www.eacea.ec.europa.eu/scholarships/erasmus-mundus-catalogue_en) lists 218 Erasmus Mundus Joint Master projects and confirms this is the central EU-level scheme: 'Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programmes are delivered by multiple higher education institutions across various countries' and students should 'visit the program's official website and directly contact the consortium for information on courses, application procedures, and scholarship availability'. The Austria-based variant is a country filter over this central EACEA catalogue spanning many different university consortia, not a single attached institution. Not applicable per batch rules for central Erasmus Mundus schemes; supervising contacts exist only on each individual consortium's programme website, which is outside this scholarship entry.

Live research (Oct 2026): The listed URL https://www.ceu.edu/scholarships returns HTTP 404; the live official pages are https://www.ceu.edu/admissions/financial-aid and https://www.ceu.edu/admissions/financial-aid/by-degree. CEU financial aid is university-wide and merit-based: the 'CEU Doctoral Scholarship, covering the full cost of tuition, complete with a monthly stipend' (Doctoral Stipend 2,002 EUR/gross/month, awarded for 48 months per the financial-aid page; the by-degree page states 1,880 EUR/gross/month), master's Tuition Awards plus Stipend Awards (300-1000 EUR/month), and bachelor Partial Tuition Awards (up to 50%, capped €4,000/year). Candidates are 'automatically considered' via the application form's Funding section; award administration sits with the Financial Aid Office (finaid@ceu.edu, Vienna office Quellenstraße 51). Like the Edinburgh Global Research Scholarship case, this is a university-wide merit award spanning 50+ degree programmes with no specific school, lab, department or supervising professor attached; no individual professor is named on any official CEU scholarship page.
